### Exploration Point 1.1: When Were Users Most Active By Hours?

> [Assumption] "TotalIntensity" is Fitbit's way of quantifying the
> overall physical effort exerted during a given hour

<br> <br>

##### *- Explore the table `intensities_hourly`*

```{r}
View(intensities_hourly)
glimpse(intensities_hourly)
```

<br> <br>

##### *- Transformation*

-   Extract the hour from the `ActivityHour` column
-   Then Sum the TotalIntensity grouped by col Id and the extracted hour
    col

```{r }
intensities_hourly_mutated <- intensities_hourly %>%
  mutate(activity_hour_extract = hour(ActivityHour))

intensities_hourly_mutated <- intensities_hourly_mutated %>%
  group_by(activity_hour_extract) %>%
  summarise(sum_total_intensity = sum(TotalIntensity)) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
# order the levels from 0 to 23 for plotting
intensities_hourly_mutated <- intensities_hourly_mutated %>%
  mutate(activity_hour_extract = factor(activity_hour_extract, levels = 0:23)) %>%
  mutate(activity_hour_extract = fct_rev(activity_hour_extract)) # Reverse the factor levels
```

<br> <br>

##### *- Plotting*

-   Horizontal bar chart

```{r}
# Create the horizontal bar chart
ggplot(intensities_hourly_mutated, aes(x = sum_total_intensity, y = activity_hour_extract)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") + # Use geom_col for pre-calculated sums, fill sets the bar color
  labs(
    title = "Activity Intensity by Hour of the Day",
    subtitle = "Each value represent the start of a 1-hour window",
    x = "Relative Intensities", # Set x-axis label to blank
    
    y = "Hour of the Day" # Label for the y-axis
  ) +
  theme_minimal() + # Start with a clean theme
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(), # Remove major grid lines
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),  # Remove minor grid lines
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),   # Remove x-axis text (number marks)
    axis.text.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = -20)) # adjusts axis text margin
  )
```

> [Observations from the above chart]\
> There are three groups of time period: peak, amping up, and winding
> down.\
> - The most easily regconizable peak intensity period is from 17:00 to
> 20:00. The second one is from 12:00 to 15:00.\
> - Amping up periods are time windows that precede the peaks and see a
> relative increase in intensity levels. Those are: "8:00 to 12:00",
> "15:00 to 17:00".\
> - Winding down periods: the rest.\
> - Worth noticing window: "15:00 to 17:00" (because it's both amping up
> and winding down).

<br> <br> <br> <br>

### Exploration Point 1.2: When Was the Peak of Calorie Burned by Hours?

> [Assumption]\
> - `calories_hourly$Calories` refers to calories burned.

<br> <br>

##### *- Explore the table `calories_hourly`*

```{r}
View(calories_hourly)
glimpse(calories_hourly)
```

<br> <br>

##### *- Transformation*

-   Extract the hour from `calories_hourly$ActivityHour`
-   Sum `calories_hourly$Calories` up by hour -\> `hour_only`
-   Factor `hour_only` for ordering on the y-axis

```{r }
hourly_calories_summary <- calories_hourly %>%
  # Ensure ActivityHour is in datetime format if it's not already
  # mutate(ActivityHour = as.POSIXct(ActivityHour)) %>% # Uncomment and adjust format if needed
  mutate(hour_only = hour(ActivityHour)) %>% # Extract the hour (0-23)
  group_by(hour_only) %>% # Group by the extracted hour
  summarise(calories_sum = sum(Calories, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>% 
  ungroup()
# We order the levels from 0 to 23
hourly_calories_summary <- hourly_calories_summary %>%
  mutate(hour_only = factor(hour_only, levels = 0:23)) %>%
  mutate(hour_only = fct_rev(hour_only)) # Reverse the factor levels so 0 is at the top
```

<br> <br>

##### *- Plotting*

-   Bar chart

```{r}
# Create the bar chart
ggplot(hourly_calories_summary, aes(x = calories_sum, y = hour_only)) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkorange") + # Use geom_col for pre-calculated sums
  labs(
    title = "Levels of Calories Burned by Hours", # Add a title
    subtitle = "Each value represent the start of a 1-hour window",
    x = "Relative Calorie Burned", # Label for the x-axis (now calories)
    y = "Hour of the Day" # Label for the y-axis (now hour)
  ) +
  theme_minimal() + # Use a clean theme
  theme(
    # Adjust theme elements for a horizontal bar chart
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),   # Remove x-axis text (number marks)
    axis.text.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = -20)) # adjusts axis text margin
  )
```

> [Observations from the above chart]\
> - The calorie-burned pattern matchs the pattern of intensity, where
> peak calorie-burned period is from 17:00 to 20:00. The second one is
> from 12:00 to 15:00.\
> - The calorie burned is quite noticeable from 21:00 to 8:00,
> considering the relatively low intensity happened during that time
> window.

### Exploration Point 2:

### 2.1 How Much Time was Spent for Active Activities

<br> <br>

##### *- Explore the table `activity_daily`*

```{r}
View(activity_daily)
glimpse(activity_daily)
```

<br> <br>

##### *- Transformation*

-   Aggregate by Id, calculate sums, count days, and calculate
    percentages
-   Transform to long format for plotting purpose

```{r}
activity_aggregated <- activity_daily %>%
  # Group the data by the 'Id' column
  group_by(Id) %>%
  # Summarise the minutes for each Id and count the number of days
  summarise(
    sum_VeryActiveMinutes = sum(VeryActiveMinutes),
    sum_FairlyActiveMinutes = sum(FairlyActiveMinutes),
    sum_LightlyActiveMinutes = sum(LightlyActiveMinutes),
    no_days = n() # Count the number of rows for each Id (assuming each row is a day)
  ) %>%
  # Calculate total active minutes and the requested percentages
  mutate(
    total_active_minutes = sum_VeryActiveMinutes + sum_FairlyActiveMinutes + sum_LightlyActiveMinutes,

    # Calculate percentage of each activity type over the total active minutes for that Id
    very_active_percent = (sum_VeryActiveMinutes / total_active_minutes) * 100,
    fairly_active_percent = (sum_FairlyActiveMinutes / total_active_minutes) * 100,
    lightly_active_percent = (sum_LightlyActiveMinutes / total_active_minutes) * 100,

    # Calculate percentage of total active minutes over the total possible minutes (days * 1440)
    active_percent_daily = (total_active_minutes / (no_days * 1440)) * 100
  ) %>%
  # Ungroup the data frame after summarising and mutating
  ungroup() 
```

```{r}
activity_pivot_long <- activity_aggregated %>%
  select(Id, very_active_percent, fairly_active_percent, lightly_active_percent, active_percent_daily) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(very_active_percent, fairly_active_percent, lightly_active_percent),
    names_to = "type_of_active_raw", # Temporary column for original names
    values_to = "type_of_active_percent"   # New column for the percentage values
  ) %>%
  # Create the 'type_of_active' column with desired labels and order
  mutate(
    type_of_active = case_when(
      type_of_active_raw == "lightly_active_percent" ~ "Lightly Active",
      type_of_active_raw == "fairly_active_percent" ~ "Fairly Active",
      type_of_active_raw == "very_active_percent" ~ "Very Active",
      TRUE ~ type_of_active_raw # Should not happen with these columns
    )
  ) %>%
  # Set the factor levels for 'type_of_active' in the desired order
  mutate(
    type_of_active = factor(type_of_active, levels = c("Lightly Active", "Fairly Active", "Very Active"))
  ) %>%
  select(-type_of_active_raw) # Remove the raw column
```

<br> <br>

##### *- Plotting*

-   Facet scatter plot

```{r, results="hide"}
# Create the correlation plot with specified facet order and coloring by group
ggplot(activity_pivot_long, aes(x = active_percent_daily, y = type_of_active_percent, color = type_of_active)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 3) + # Use points for a scatter plot, alpha for transparency
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 25)) + # control the x-axis limits
  facet_wrap(~ type_of_active) + # Facet by type_of_active (now ordered)
  # Manually set colors for each activity type
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Lightly Active" = "cornflowerblue",  # Lighter shade for Lightly Active
      "Fairly Active" = "steelblue",   # Medium shade for Fairly Active
      "Very Active" = "darkblue"       # Darker shade for Very Active
    ),
    guide = "none" # Remove the legend for color since it's faceted by type already
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Relationship between Active Activity Types and Active Activity Time",
    x = "Proportion of active time over a day", 
    y = "Proportion of active types"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() + # Clean theme
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", size = 0.5), # Keep light grid lines for readability within facets
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), # Remove minor grid lines
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"), # Make facet titles bold
    legend.position = "none" # no color legend
  )
```

> [Observations from the above chart]\
> - There's no correlation between active types and daily time spent for
> active activities.  

<br>

-   Histogram

```{r}
# Create the histogram of active_percent_daily
ggplot(activity_aggregated, aes(x = active_percent_daily)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") + # Create the histogram bars
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 25, by = 5)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 25, by = 5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "How Users Spent Time for Active Activities Daily",
    subtitle = "Bin width = [0, 5]%, (5, 10]%, (10, 15]%, etc.",
    x = "Proportion of Time Spent Daily (%)",
    y = "User Count" # Label for the y-axis
  ) +
  theme_minimal() + # Use a clean theme
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),  # Remove minor vertical grid lines
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank()  # Remove minor vertical grid lines
  )
```

> [Observations from the above chart]\
> - The amount of time spent for active activities daily is equal to 15%
> on average.\
> - The range from 10% to 20% daily time spent for active activities is
> the most popular.

### 2.2 When Users Were Active, Which Level of Activeness Did Users Spend Time For the Most?

<br> <br>

##### *- Transformation*

```{r}
# Calculate the mean percentage for each activity type and prepare data for stacking and labels
for_stacked_bar <- activity_pivot_long %>%
  # Group by the activity type
  group_by(type_of_active) %>%
  # Summarise to calculate the mean percentage for each group
  summarise(
    MeanPercentage = mean(type_of_active_percent, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>% # Ungroup the data
  # Arrange by type_of_active factor levels for correct stacking
  arrange(type_of_active) %>%
  # Calculate the position for the text labels within the stacked bars
  # This requires calculating cumulative sums
  mutate(
    # Calculate the cumulative sum of percentages
    cumulative_percentage = cumsum(MeanPercentage),
    # Calculate the text position as the midpoint of each segment
    text_position = MeanPercentage / 2 + lag(cumulative_percentage, default = 0)
  )
```

<br> <br>

##### *- Plotting*

-   Stacked bar chart

```{r }
# Create the base stacked bar chart
stacked_bar_chart_annotate <- ggplot(for_stacked_bar, aes(x = "", y = MeanPercentage, fill = type_of_active)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.5) + # Create the stacked bar
  labs(
    title = "Which Level of Activeness Did Users Spend Time For the Most?", # Add a title
    x = "", # Remove x-axis label
    y = "Average Percentage", # Y-axis label
    fill = "Activity Types" # Title for the legend
  ) +
  theme_minimal() + # Use a clean theme
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_blank(), # Remove x-axis title
    axis.text.x = element_blank(), # Remove x-axis text (since it's a single bar)
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(), # Remove major grid lines
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), # Remove minor grid lines
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.6),# Center the plot title
    legend.position = "top", # Position the legend
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, -170, "pt") # left-aligned
  )

# Add data labels using annotate() for manual adjustment
# You will need to manually adjust the 'y' coordinate for each label
stacked_bar_chart_annotate <- stacked_bar_chart_annotate +
  # Label for Lightly Active
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = "", # X-position (center of the bar)
    y = for_stacked_bar$text_position[for_stacked_bar$type_of_active == "Lightly Active"], # Calculated Y-position
    label = paste0(round(for_stacked_bar$MeanPercentage[for_stacked_bar$type_of_active == "Lightly Active"], 1), "%"), # Formatted percentage
    color = "black", # Label color (adjust as needed for visibility)
    size = 4 # Label size
    # Use vjust and hjust here if further fine-tuning is needed
  ) +
  # Label for Fairly Active
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = "", # X-position (center of the bar)
    y = for_stacked_bar$text_position[for_stacked_bar$type_of_active == "Fairly Active"], # Calculated Y-position
    label = paste0(round(for_stacked_bar$MeanPercentage[for_stacked_bar$type_of_active == "Fairly Active"], 1), "%"), # Formatted percentage
    color = "black", # Label color (adjust as needed for visibility)
    size = 4, # Label size
    vjust = 19
    # Use vjust and hjust here if further fine-tuning is needed
  ) +
  # Label for Very Active
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = "", # X-position (center of the bar)
    y = for_stacked_bar$text_position[for_stacked_bar$type_of_active == "Very Active"], # Calculated Y-position
    label = paste0(round(for_stacked_bar$MeanPercentage[for_stacked_bar$type_of_active == "Very Active"], 1), "%"), # Formatted percentage
    color = "black", # Label color (adjust as needed for visibility)
    size = 4, # Label size
    vjust = 23
    # Use vjust and hjust here if further fine-tuning is needed
  ) +
  # Add the "100%" note inside the plot
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = "", # X-position (center of the bar)
    y = 105, # Y-position (adjust this value to place the note correctly)
    label = "(100% of time)",
    vjust = 0, # Vertical justification
    hjust = 0.5, # Horizontal justification
    size = 4,
    color = "black"
  )
stacked_bar_chart_annotate
```

> [Observations from the above chart]\
> - The lightly active activities occupies a major proportion (84.9%),
> dominating the two other types of active activites.

### Exploration Point 3: How Many Hours per Day Did Users Sleep

<br> <br>

##### *- Explore the table `sleep_minute`*

```{r}
View(sleep_minute)
glimpse(sleep_minute)
```

<br> <br>

##### *- Transformation*

-   From the `sleep_minute` table, extract date only from the date time
    column `date`, then group the `Id` and `date_only` columns and
    aggregate (sum) the `value` column to have `sleep_minute_daily` -\>
    result in `aggregated_sleep_minute` table
-   From `aggregated_sleep_minute` table, group `Id` column then take
    the average of `sleep_minute_daily` -\> result in
    `mean_sleep_minute` table

```{r }
# Step 1 & 2: Extract date and group by Id and date, then aggregate (sum) sleep minutes daily
# Resulting table: aggregated_sleep_minute
aggregated_sleep_minute <- sleep_minute %>%
  # Ensure the 'date' column is in datetime format if it's not already
  # mutate(date = as.POSIXct(date)) %>% # Uncomment and adjust format if needed
  mutate(date_only = as.Date(date)) %>% # Extract date only
  group_by(Id, date_only) %>% # Group by Id and the extracted date
  summarise(sleep_minute_daily = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>% # Sum the sleep minutes daily, .groups = 'drop' removes grouping
  ungroup() # Ensure ungrouping (redundant with .groups='drop' but good practice)

# Step 3 & 4: Group by Id from aggregated_sleep_minute and take the average of sleep_minute_daily
# Resulting table: mean_sleep_minute
mean_sleep_minute <- aggregated_sleep_minute %>%
  group_by(Id) %>% # Group by Id
  summarise(mean_sleep_minute = mean(sleep_minute_daily, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>% # Calculate the average daily sleep minutes per Id
  ungroup() # Ensure ungrouping

# Print the resulting tables (optional, for verification)
# print("Aggregated Daily Sleep Minutes:")
# print(aggregated_sleep_minute)
# print("Mean Daily Sleep Minutes per User:")
# print(mean_sleep_minute)
```

<br> <br>

##### *- Plotting*

-   Histogram

```{r}
ggplot(mean_sleep_minute, aes(x = mean_sleep_minute/60)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 3
                 , fill = "skyblue", color = "white", alpha = 0.8) + 
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 15, by = 3)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 30, by = 2)) +
  labs(
    title = "Sleep Habits of Users", 
    subtitle = "Bin width = [0, 3], (3, 6], (6, 9], etc.",
    x = "Average Daily Sleep Hours", 
    y = "User Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), # Remove major vertical grid lines
  ) 
```

> [Observations from the above chart]\
> - Most of the users already had a decent amount of sleep hours (more
> than 6 hours per day).\
> - Suprisingly the group of users who had 9-to-12-hour sleep is the
> peak.

### 4.2 How Intense Were the Distance-based Exercises

> [Assumption]\
> - LightActiveDistance: includes leisurely walking or other low-effort
> movements.\
> - ModeratelyActiveDistance: includes activities like brisk walking,
> moderate cycling, or other activities that elevate your heart rate and
> breathing somewhat but where you can still hold a conversation.\
> - VeryActiveDistance: includes activities like running, high-intensity
> interval training (HIIT), or other strenuous efforts where you are
> breathing heavily and finding it difficult to speak in full sentences.

<br> <br>

##### *- Transformation*

-   Calculate the proportion of summed up distance groups
-   Then transform to long format for treemap plot

```{r }
# Calculate the sum of each activity distance column across all rows
distance_sums <- activity_daily %>%
  summarise(
    SumVeryActiveDistance = sum(VeryActiveDistance, na.rm = TRUE),
    SumModeratelyActiveDistance = sum(ModeratelyActiveDistance, na.rm = TRUE),
    SumLightActiveDistance = sum(LightActiveDistance, na.rm = TRUE),
    SumSedentaryActiveDistance = sum(SedentaryActiveDistance, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
# This sum will be used as the denominator for calculating proportions
sum_of_components <- distance_sums$SumVeryActiveDistance +
                     distance_sums$SumModeratelyActiveDistance +
                     distance_sums$SumLightActiveDistance +
                     distance_sums$SumSedentaryActiveDistance

# Prepare data frame for treemap plot
# Need to use pivot_longer to transform into long format
# Calculate the percentage here, which will be used in the label
treemap_data <- distance_sums %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(), # Select all columns (the sum columns)
    names_to = "ActivityTypeRaw", # Temporary column for the original column names
    values_to = "TotalDistanceSum" # New column for the total distance sum for each type
  ) %>%
  # Clean up the ActivityType names and create the final ActivityType column
  mutate(
    ActivityType = case_when(
      ActivityTypeRaw == "SumVeryActiveDistance" ~ "Very Active",
      ActivityTypeRaw == "SumModeratelyActiveDistance" ~ "Moderately Active",
      ActivityTypeRaw == "SumLightActiveDistance" ~ "Light Active",
      ActivityTypeRaw == "SumSedentaryActiveDistance" ~ "Sedentary Active",
    ),
    # Calculate the percentage of each activity type relative to the sum of components
    # This percentage is calculated BEFORE plotting and added as a column
    Percentage = round((TotalDistanceSum / sum_of_components) * 100, 1)
    ) %>%
  select(ActivityType, Percentage)
# Pre-compile labels for the plot
treemap_data <- treemap_data %>%
  mutate(
    Label = paste(
      ActivityType," Distance",
      "\n", 
      Percentage, "%",
      sep = ""
    )
  )
```

<br> <br>

##### *- Plotting*

-   Treemap

```{r}
# Custom color assignments (reversed RdYlGn with manual selection)
custom_colors <- brewer.pal(11, "RdYlGn")[c(5, 3, 11, 1)]  # Red, orange, light orange, green
names(custom_colors) <- c("Very Active", "Moderately Active", "Light Active", "Sedentary Active")

# Ensure your treemap_data is ordered correctly (critical for color matching)
treemap_data <- treemap_data %>%
  mutate(ActivityType = factor(ActivityType, levels = names(custom_colors))) %>%
  arrange(ActivityType)

# Create treemap with manual colors
treemap(
  treemap_data,
  index = "Label",          # Use precomputed labels
  vSize = "Percentage",     # Box sizes
  title = "Distance Breakdown By Activities (Sedentary Active Distance 0.01% not plotted)",
  fontsize.title = 14,
  fontsize.labels = 12,
  fontcolor.labels = "black",
  border.col = "white",
  palette = custom_colors,             # Color palette
  inflate.labels = TRUE           # Ensure labels are visible
)
```

> [Observations from the above chart]\
> - Lightly active level has a 62.2% share of the total distance.\
> - Moderately active (10.5%) and very active (27.2%) levels are also
> noticeable.\
> - Sedentary active level (0.01%) is minuscule.
